content:
As a business owner, your priority is simple: driving profit. When hiring a virtual assistant, the goal isn’t simply to alleviate busyness but to unlock smarter operations so that revenue‑generating efforts take centre stage.

As the virtual assistant industry continues to develop and expand, it becomes increasingly important to discern the quality of your partner and the person you bring on board.

This article explores the do’s and don’ts or the green signals to look for and the red flags to heed when you are outsourcing support functions.

Why Are Businesses Outsourcing Virtual Assistants?

Businesses hire virtual assistants primarily to save time, money and increase efficiency, not merely because they’re busy.

By outsourcing routine duties, such as email and calendar management, data entry, or basic customer service, business leaders free themselves to focus on core tasks like sales, customer development and strategy. The extra hours gained from hiring a virtual assistant can be used to generate new business and greater revenue to achieve new heights.

Various surveys support this sentiment. In a recent one, it is said that companies using assistants found an average 28% jump in productivity. In the same study, outsourcing remote professionals was cited as the reason why almost half of managers saw their weekly workloads cut by 10+ hours.

Overall, these numbers convey how delegating even a few hours of admin or specialised support can yield a significant return on investment.

Red Flags or the Don’t’s: Warning Signs of a Poor Virtual Assistant Provider

When evaluating virtual assistant agencies or companies, watch for any of the following warning signs. These red flags often indicate a provider may be unprofessional, unreliable, or risky:

Overpromising 24/7 Coverage

Be skeptical of claims like “24/7 always-on support” if the provider can’t explain how it works. A reliable virtual assistant service often does not compromise the well-being of the remote professional they hired, because doing so may affect the quality of their work. And, in turn, negatively affect the tasks you delegated to them.

Poor Communication or Responsiveness

Note how the company treats you during the sales process. If they are slow to respond, give canned answers, or fail to answer basic questions (like how they recruit or integrity of the hiring process, etc). This lack of communication will only worsen if you appoint them.

Absence of Team Leaders or Managers

One sign of low quality is when an agency has too many virtual assistants with little to virtually no managing parties or support system in place.

Without team leaders or managers ensuring smooth communication and coordination between the client and assistant, delegated tasks may miss deadlines or not meet the exact specifications you requested.

Negative Reviews or Controversies

A quick web search can reveal problems. Consistent complaints about missed deadlines, billing issues, or breaches of trust are definite red flags. Any news of data breaches or legal matters involving the provider should be taken as a severe warning.

If you encounter any of the above, it’s wise to reconsider. It’s far better to spot a problematic provider early than to deal with issues after signing on.

Green Signals: Positive Indicators of a Good VA Provider

Dedicated Point of Contact

Good virtual assistant agencies like Virtual Office Angels assign you a main account manager or contact person. This manager coordinates your assistant’s work and is your go-to for questions or issues. A single point of contact means continuity and direct accountability.

The provider should also assure you that supervisors or team leaders manage your assistant’s workload, so no one is left without support which ensures sustainability and VA retention.

Relevant Expertise

The provider’s assistants should be experienced in areas important to you. They should only vet candidates with real hands-on expertise and familiarity with the tools and processes generally used in your industry. They should also explain their recruiting process (e.g., skills tests, interviews, background checks, etc).  It is important to note that training your VA is not your job as this is one big time consuming factor that often is left unseen. 

Industry-Specific Support

Many providers offer specialised assistants for specific industries. For instance, some agencies match clients with virtual loans assistantswho are highly adept in every aspect of mortgage processing. Others provide VAs who can handle financial admin or bookkeeping.

If your field has specific jargon or compliance rules, a provider that emphasises niche expertise is a major plus.

Robust Security and Tech-savvy

A green provider will proactively protect your data. Expect them to sign NDAs and use secure collaboration tools (encrypted storage, secure password managers, two-factor authentication, etc.). They should also be fluent in communication and project-management platforms.

Final Thoughts

Outsourcing to a reliable virtual assistant can be transformative for businesses growth. However, it’s only possible if the partnership is managed wisely. Keep in mind that every outsourcing decision carries both opportunities and risks.

By watching out for the red flags outlined above and seeking the green signals of a reputable agency, you give your venture the best chance of success.
